The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors $\{i,j\}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{i,j\}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -7 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
The linear transformation $\mathbf T$ has the standard matrix 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154685/assets/6a14933078db8802426a1ab22ba692e17fd6f795ec4bd746a6fb16687aa441ed.svg) 
What are the images of the standard basis vectors $\{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ under the action of $\mathbf T?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot\mathbf{i}$ and $T\cdot\mathbf{j}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 \\ 8 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 \\ 8 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
To construct the standard matrix of a linear transformation $T$ in $\mathbb{R}^2,$ we find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ under $T,$ and then use those images as columns in the standard matrix.

To demonstrate, let's consider the following linear transformation: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154685/assets/b399f02949935d4a4425b19e4946a3eb47375272bb0271586c93da504ff0bd2e.svg)

Computing $\mathbf T(\mathbf i),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\cdot 1-1\cdot 0 \\ 1+3\cdot 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $\mathbf T(\mathbf j),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\cdot 0-1\cdot 1 \\ 0+3\cdot 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154685/assets/be0afb6703a6d5e4bcbb360297240a74f4aeec7efbbb1229c8cd01e112fa6bda.svg)

In the diagram below, we see the vectors in the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and their images $\{ \mathbf{i'}, \mathbf{j'} \}$ under the transformation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154685/assets/9189a79fe44936221e38e7c051f9f0ddd53338c80cd324ba804d61beef6c2c44.png)

In general, a linear transformation in $\mathbb R^n$ has a standard matrix of dimensions $n \times n,$ whose columns are the images of the basis vectors under the action of the linear transformation.

tutorials.title: Introduction
tutorials.content:
To construct the standard matrix of a linear transformation $T$ in $\mathbb{R}^2,$ we find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ under $T,$ and then use those images as columns in the standard matrix.

To demonstrate, let's consider the following linear transformation: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154685/assets/b399f02949935d4a4425b19e4946a3eb47375272bb0271586c93da504ff0bd2e.svg)

Computing $\mathbf T(\mathbf i),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\cdot 1-1\cdot 0 \\ 1+3\cdot 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $\mathbf T(\mathbf j),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\cdot 0-1\cdot 1 \\ 0+3\cdot 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154685/assets/be0afb6703a6d5e4bcbb360297240a74f4aeec7efbbb1229c8cd01e112fa6bda.svg)

In the diagram below, we see the vectors in the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and their images $\{ \mathbf{i'}, \mathbf{j'} \}$ under the transformation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14154685/assets/9189a79fe44936221e38e7c051f9f0ddd53338c80cd324ba804d61beef6c2c44.png)

In general, a linear transformation in $\mathbb R^n$ has a standard matrix of dimensions $n \times n,$ whose columns are the images of the basis vectors under the action of the linear transformation.
